entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: An individual person named in the text, whatever their employer (such as researchers, accountants, technicians, engineers, officials, vendor representatives and residents); does not include teams, offices or other organizations.

entity_types.name: Pump
entity_types.description: A water pump unit or pumping assembly (such as station duty pumps or flume pumps); does not include non-pump scientific instruments, civil infrastructure, or tools.

entity_types.name: Equipment
entity_types.description: A non-pump mechanical device, scientific apparatus, tool, or component part (such as sediment flumes, soil corers, mechanical seals, and intake screens); does not include water pumps.

entity_types.name: Place
entity_types.description: A physical location, geographic site, station, room, street, or civil structure (such as Aldmoor bog, North Station, Mill Lane footbridge, Eastgate library, or room B12); does not include organizations or events.

entity_types.name: Event
entity_types.description: A time-bounded occurrence, scheduled activity, meeting, conference, talk, inspection round, failure incident, or municipal works project; does not include static places or continuous facilities.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A formal collective entity such as an institute team, municipal council, utility authority, or commercial vendor (such as Soil Ecology, Riverton Town Council, Riverton Water, or Calder Pumps); does not include individual persons or physical facilities.

fact_types.description: The pump is physically situated, installed, or operated at the specified place or station.
The equipment or apparatus is housed, deployed, or situated at the specified location.
The event occurred at, or the works project altered, the specified location.
The person resides at, works at, operates a business at, or is located on the specified place.
The person attended, presented at, chaired, spoke at, inspected during, conducted fieldwork in, or performed work on the event.
The person belongs to, works in, is employed by, serves on, or represents the team, office, council, utility or vendor.
The person serves as group leader or direct supervisor of the other person.
The person drives, frees, handles, or uses the equipment or apparatus.
The technician or engineer inspected, repaired, replaced seals on, regreased, or isolated the pump.
The seal kit, bearing, or screen belongs to, is installed on, or is specified as a replacement part for the pump.
The organization sponsors, organizes, votes on, or oversees the project or event.
The maintenance round, work order, incident, or test run acted upon or evaluated the pump.
The coring trip, commissioning run, or experiment utilized or investigated the piece of equipment.
A quantitative operational or diagnostic metric for the pump, such as flow rate, temperature, vibration, or runtime.
A quantitative dimension, operating limit, or threshold of the equipment, such as length or vibration limit.
A quantitative environmental or structural parameter measured at the location, such as core depth, pH, water table level, or board count.
A monetary expenditure, budget line, contract value, or overrun recorded for the project or event.
A quoted price, unit cost, or purchase expenditure for the piece of equipment or replacement component.
